articleTitle: Hierarchical test strategy planning based on cost evaluation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: The need for design for testability (DFT) is now widely accepted as an important part of integrated circuit design. The proposed test planner seeks to aid the designer in choosing the optimum DFT strategy for a particular design, keeping in mind market trends and company resources. A knowledge base is used to hold test method data, which are compared using a hierarchical, parametrised cost model. An inference engine will use the results of a testability analysis of the design blocks together with the knowledge base and the cost model predictions to make heuristic DFT choices, which will then be evaluated. The test planner will be linked with design tools for easy transfer of design information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with an expert diagnostic system shell
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: Efficient diagnosis and repair of failing electronic circuit boards is essential for a major telecommunications company, such as British Telecom. This is particularly true of complex high volume cards found in the new digital exchanges. Some boards comprise mixed analogue and digital circuitry and technologically advanced components such as Subscriber Line Interface Circuits. As such, they are not amenable to the well-established back-tracing diagnostic techniques developed for purely digital circuitry. The traditional approach to diagnosis, that of deploying technicians armed with 'rack and stack' equipment, is costly in terms of manpower and equipment, and is critically dependent on the availability of skilled labour. The goal of the work described in this paper was to achieve a substantial cost reduction in the diagnosis of mixed signal boards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: A single test generation tool cannot generate tests for today's designs unless designers are prepared to restrict themselves to certain limited types of circuitry. In general therefore, a number of test generation tools is required and to gain maximum benefit the tools should cooperate in an integrated environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solutions to the problems of test vector translation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: Describes an intelligent translator that enables design validation waveforms for a digital design to be used as the basis of test programs on multiple pieces of automatic test equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low cost PC-based functional test system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: Outlines the make-up of a typical low-cost 'rack and stack' system and the necessary software development to implement a functional test on a small analogue circuit board.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The link from automated circuit design to fault testing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: Focusses on the role of the Exon system in the design and test process for digital circuits. The first section outlines the Exon system and its relation to professional software. The next section considers the programs of the system in operation. Finally example circuits and results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge representation automaton for functional test schedules (KRAFTS)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Computer Aided Test and Diagnosis
abstract: CAD-generated component and interconnection listings are utilised to recreate a circuit design in the form of an associative network. This is stored within an expert systems' database and enables a powerful search algorithm, under the guidance of testability formulation rules, to explore the circuit. The algorithm interacts with these device models and register transfer logic based device operation rules to identify valid test paths through a circuit and thus define functional tests. Once identified, the tests are ordered (using rule-based and heuristic techniques) in terms of increasing test complexity to aid diagnostics. Finally, the test paths are passed on to a low-level test timing generator to produce the actual test vectors required to test the board.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
